answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with sponsored admission: a newcomer enters only through a sponsor who stakes one of a few earned invitation slots, and the slot returns only after the newcomer completes attested work. Like pigment settling in a lagoon, trust accumulates slowly and cannot be rushed; each fake identity costs a slot and real work, so the price of an army of echoes grows with every copy while honest agents sponsor only those they would vouch for.
